title: AIPerf's machine-readable export — the record a bench_result is built on
description:
Mission M2.2.1: 'bench_result 应该有 jsonl 或者 json，然后有针对该 json 校验的 schema'. AIPerf writes four things at the end of a run — a CSV, a JSON export, a rendered console table, and a gzipped per-request JSONL. **The JSON export is the record and the other three are renderings of it**: the CSV carries the same metrics with the percentile columns blanked out wherever AIPerf did not compute them (measured: `sum` and `p1..p25` are empty strings for every throughput row), the console text is the CSV formatted with box-drawing characters and thousands separators, and the JSONL is the per-request detail the summary was computed from. So this schema is written against `items/result/profile_export_aiperf.json`, which is the only one of the four that is lossless and typed.

Written against the real sealed artefact at `cheat_for_mock/stage2-profiling/aiperf_baseline/content/items/result/profile_export_aiperf.json` (aiperf 0.12.0, export schema_version 1.4, 721 requests) and cross-checked against `aiperf_profiled/`, which is the same load against a CUDA-graph-off deployment and therefore the same shape with different numbers.

**The one rule from `assets/schemas/README.md` this file departs from is `additionalProperties: false` at the top level, and the departure is argued rather than lazy.** That rule exists because 'an open schema that accepts a typo is never noticed' — but this document is not hand-written, it is a machine export from a third-party tool that adds metrics between releases (0.12.0 already carries 60 top-level metrics, twelve of them `replay_*` and `active_*` names that did not exist in 0.10). A typo is not a failure mode here; a closed schema would be. Every metric the sealed export carries is still enumerated below, so the schema documents the export rather than merely admitting it, and `schema_version` is pinned to a known set so that an incompatible format change stops the pipeline here instead of at whatever reads a renamed field next.

schema_version.description: AIPerf's own export format version, pinned. A bump is not automatically wrong, and it is not something a downstream reader may discover by finding a field missing — the schema is where somebody looks at the new format and adds the version deliberately.

was_cancelled.description: Required, and required to be present rather than required to be false. A cancelled run is a legitimate artefact to keep; what is not legitimate is a reader that cannot tell. `check_bench_result` is what refuses it.

error_summary.description: AIPerf's own error accounting. Present and empty on a clean run. It is deliberately NOT the thing the error rate is computed from — that is read per-request from profile_export.jsonl.gz, because this field's shape has moved between AIPerf releases and a missing key reads as zero errors, which is the one wrong answer that looks like success.

run_info.description: What was actually run. `cli_command` is the whole invocation, and it is required because it is the only field in the export that says which endpoint, which tokenizer and which trace produced these numbers — everything else is the numbers themselves.

input_config.description: The load's own configuration as AIPerf resolved it — not as the caller wrote it. This is where 'the bench ran against the deployment we think it did' is checkable, and it is the half a summary of the numbers cannot replace.

streaming.description: Not required, and it matters: with streaming off AIPerf reports no inter-token latency and no TTFT, so a non-streaming export is a legitimate document that cannot answer the questions stage 2 exists to ask. `check_bench_result` is where that becomes a refusal.

scalar_metric.description: A metric AIPerf computes once for the whole run — a count, a throughput, a duration. It carries no distribution because there is nothing to distribute over.

sampled_metric.description: A metric sampled over time rather than per request — concurrency, in-flight tokens, instantaneous throughput. It has percentiles and a spread but no `count` and no `sum`, because the sample population is time slices and neither figure would mean anything.

distribution_metric.description:
A per-request metric: every request contributes one observation, so there is a `count` and a `sum` as well as the percentiles.

**`count` is required and it is the load-bearing field.** AIPerf exits 0 when its schedule window turns out to contain nothing, and then every export is present, every file is well-formed, and the whole thing describes zero requests. A shape check passes that. `check_bench_result` reads this count against a floor, and the floor is why the export is worth having a schema for at all.
